questions.q: Let sets $A$~and $B$ have $5$ elements each. Let the mean of the elements in sets $A$~and $B$~be~$5$~and $8$ respectively and the variance of the elements in sets $A$ and $B$ be $12$ and $20$ respectively. A new set $C$ of $10$ elements is formed by subtracting $3$ from each element of $A$ and adding $2$ to each element of $B$. Then the sum of the mean and variance of the elements of~$C$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the elements in set& $A$~be~\left\{{x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, {x}_{3}, {x}_{4}, {x}_{5}\right\}$

Now given mean is$= 5$

Now subtracting~$3$~from each term we get,~

New mean as~\left({x}_{1} - 3, {x}_{2} - 3 \ldots , {x}_{5} - 3\right) = 5 - 3 = 2$

So, sum of elements will be~$2 \times 5 = 10$

Also given variance,

$Var \left(X\right) = 12$

Now we know that subtracting~$3$~from each term will not change the variance,

So,~$Var \left({x}_{1} - 3, {x}_{2} - 3, \ldots {x}_{5} - 3\right) = 12$

$⇒ \dfrac{∑ \left({x}_{i} - 3\right)2}{5} - 4 = 12$

$⇒ ∑ \left({x}_{i} - 3\right)2 = 80$

Now let elements in set~$B$~be~\left\{{y}_{1}, {y}_{2} \ldots {y}_{5}\right\}$

Given mean~\left({y}_{1}, {y}_{2} \ldots {y}_{5}\right) = 8$

Now adding each element by $2$~we get,

New mean \left({y}_{1} + 2, {y}_{2} + 2, \ldots {y}_{5} + 2\right) = 10$

So, sum of elements will be~$10 \times 5 = 50$

Also given~$Var \left({y}_{1}, {y}_{2} \ldots {y}_{5}\right) = 20$

Similarly new variance,~

$Var \left({y}_{1} + 2, {y}_{2} + 2 \ldots {y}_{5} + 2\right) = 20$

$⇒ \dfrac{∑ \left({y}_{i} + 2\right)2}{5} - 100 = 20$

$⇒ ∑ \left({y}_{i} + 2\right)2 = 120 \times 5$

Now finding, combined mean we get,

$\dfrac{{∑}_{i = 1}^{5}\left({x}_{i} - 3\right) + ∑ \left({y}_{i} + 2\right)}{10}= \dfrac{10 + 50}{10} = 6$

And combined variance~$= \dfrac{∑ \left({x}_{i} - 3\right)2 + ∑ \left({y}_{i} + 2\right)2}{10} - {6}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{80 + 120 \times 5}{10} - 36 = 32$

Hence, the sum of combined mean and variance will be~$32 + 6 = 38$

$

questions.q: The mean and standard deviation of 20 observations are found to be 10 and 2 . respectively. On rechecking, it was found that an observation by mistake was taken 8 instead of 12. The correct standard deviation is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Mean }(\overline{\mathrm{x}})=10 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}}{20}=10 \\ & \Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}=10 \times 20=200 \end{aligned}$
If 8 is replaced by 12, then $\Sigma x_i=200-8+12=204\therefore$ Correct mean $(\overline{\mathrm{x}})=\frac{\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}}{20}=\frac{204}{20}=10.2\because$ Standard deviation $=2\therefore$ Variance $=(\text { S.D. })^2=2^2=4\Rightarrow \frac{\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2}{20}-\left(\frac{\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}}{20}\right)^2=4\Rightarrow \frac{\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2}{20}-(10)^2=4\Rightarrow \frac{\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2}{20}=104\Rightarrow \Sigma x_i^2=2080$
Now, replaced ' 8 ' observations by ' 12 ' Then, $\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2=2080-8^2+12^2=2160\therefore$ Variance of removing observations $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{\Sigma x_i^2}{20}-\left(\frac{\Sigma x_i}{20}\right)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2160}{20}-(10.2)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 108-104.04 \\ & \Rightarrow 3.96 \end{aligned}$
Correct standard deviation $=\sqrt{3.96}$

questions.q: The mean and the variance of five observations are $4$ and $5.20$, respectively. If three of the observations are $3, 4$ and $4$; then the absolute value of the difference of the other two observations, is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let rest two observations are $x$~and~$y$.

Given mean~$= 4$

$⇒ \dfrac{3 + 4 + 4 + x + y}{5} = 4 ⇒ x + y = 9 . . . \left(1\right)$

Given variance~$= 5 . 2$

$⇒ $\dfrac{9 + 16 + 16 + x^{2} + y^{2}}{5} - \left(4\right)2 = 5 . 2$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} = 65 . . . \left(2\right)$

Squaring equation~ \left(1\right)$~and subtracting equation~ \left(2\right)$, we get

$2xy = 81 - 65 ⇒ 2xy = 16 ⇒ xy = 8$

$∴ \left(x - y\right)2 = x^{2} + y^{2} - 2xy = 65 - 16 = 49$

$∴ \left|x - y\right| = 7$

$

questions.q: A data consists of $n$ observations: ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, \ldots , {x}_{n} .$ If $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}\left({x}_{i} + 1\right)2 = 9n$~and $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}\left({x}_{i} - 1\right)2 = 5n$, then the standard deviation of this data is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}\left({x}_{i} + 1\right)2 = 9n$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n} \left({x}_i^{2} +$2{x}_{i} + 1\right) = 9n . . . \left(1\right)$

And,~$\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}\left({x}_{i} -$1\right)2 = 5n$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n} \left({x}_i^{2} -$2{x}_{i} + 1\right) = 5n . . . \left(2\right)$~

Form \left($1\right) + \left(2\right)$,~we get

$\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n} \left(2{x}_i^{2} + 2\right) = 14n$~

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_i^{2} = 6n . . . \left(3\right)$

From~ \left($1\right) - \left(2\right)$,~we get~

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_{i} = n . . . \left($4\right)$

$∴$ Variance, ${σ}^{2} = $E\left($x^{2}\right) - $\lleft(E\left(x\right)\right)2$

$⇒ {σ}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ x^{2}}{n} - \dfrac{∑ x}{n}$

$⇒ {σ}^{2} = \dfrac{6n}{n} - \left(\dfrac{n}{n}\right)$2 = 6 - 1 = 5$

$∴$~Standard deviation, \sigma = \sqrt{5}.

$

questions.q: Let $9 = {x}_{1} < {x}_{2} < \ldots < {x}_{7}$~be in an A.P. with common difference $d$. If the standard deviation of ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2} \ldots , {x}_{7}$~is 4 and the mean is $\overset{¯}{x}$, then $\overset{¯}{x} + {x}_{6}$& is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$9 = {x}_{1} < {x}_{2} < \ldots < {x}_{7}$~be in an A.P. with common difference $d$

And~the standard deviation of ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2} \ldots , {x}_{7}$~is 4 and the mean is $\overset{¯}{x}$,

Now solving,~$9 = {x}_{1} < {x}_{2} < \ldots \ldots < {x}_{7}$~which is an A.P, we get,

$9, 9 + d, 9 + 2d, \ldots \ldots \ldots . 9 + 6d$

Now subtracting~$9$~from the series we get,

$0, d, 2d, . . . . . . . 6d$

So, mean will be~$\overset{¯}{x}new = \dfrac{21d}{7} = 3d$

Now using the formula of variance we get,

${σ}^{2} = \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}\left({x}_{i}\right)2 - \left(\overset{¯}{x}\right)2$

$⇒ 16 = \dfrac{1}{7}\left({0}^{2} + {1}^{2} + \ldots \ldots . . + {6}^{2}\right)d^{2} - 9d^{2}$

$⇒ 16 = \dfrac{1}{7}\left(\dfrac{6 \times 7 \times 13}{6}\right)d^{2} - 9d^{2}$

$⇒ 16 = 4d^{2}$

$⇒ d^{2} = 4$

$⇒ d = 2$

So, mean~$\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{9 + 9 + d + 9 + 2d \ldots \ldots \ldots . 9 + 6d}{7} = 15$

Hence,~$\overset{¯}{x} + {x}_{6} = 15 + 9 + 5d = 15 + 9 + 10 = 34$

questions.solution:
Given,

The mean of the below data is& $5$

$x$ $1$ $3$ $5$ $7$ $9$
Frequency~ \left(f\right)$ $4$ $24$ $28$ $\alpha$ $8$

Now finding mean we get,

$\dfrac{4 + 72 + 28 \times 5 + 7\alpha + 72}{64 + \alpha} = 5$

$⇒ \alpha = 16$

So, total number of observation will be,~$∑ {f}_{i} = 80$

Now finding, mean deviation we get,

$M . D = \dfrac{∑ {f}_{i}\left|{x}_{i} - 5\right|}{∑ {f}_{i}}$

$= \dfrac{4 \times 4 + 24 \times 2 + 0 + 16 \times 2 + 8 \times 4}{80}= \dfrac{8}{5}$

So,~$m = \dfrac{8}{5}$

Now finding, variance we get,~

${σ}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {f}_{i}\left|{x}_{i} - 5\right|2}{∑ {f}_{i}}$

Hence, the value of~$\dfrac{3\alpha}{m + {σ}^{2}} = \dfrac{3 \times 16}{\dfrac{8}{5} + \dfrac{22}{5}} = 8$

$

questions.q: Let ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, {x}_{3}, \ldots . . , {x}_{20}$ be in geometric progression with ${x}_{1} = 3$ and the common ration $\dfrac{1}{2}$. A new data is constructed replacing each ${x}_{i}$ by \left({x}_{i} - i\right)2$. If $x$ is the mean of new data, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, {x}_{3}, \ldots . . , {x}_{20}$~are in G.P with common difference~$\dfrac{1}{2}$~and first term as~$3$

Now using the formula for sum of G.P we get,

$\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{20}{x}_{i} = \dfrac{3 \left(1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$20\right)}{1 - $\dfrac{1}{2}} = $6\left($1 - $\dfrac{1}{220}\right)

Now new sum of G.P with new data will be$= \mathop{∑}_{i = $1}^{20} \left({x}_{i} -i\right)2$

$= \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{20}\left({x}_{i}\right)$2 + \left(i\right)2 - 2{x}_{i}i$

Now~$\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{20}\left({x}_{i}\right)$2 = \dfrac{9 \left(1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$20\right)}${1 - $\dfrac{1}{4}} $=12 \left($1 - \dfrac{1}{240}\right)$

And~$\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{20}i^{2} = \dfrac{1}{6} \times20 \times21 \times41 = 2870$

And~$\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{20}{x}_{i}i = 3 + 2 . 3\dfrac{1}{2} +3 . 3\dfrac{1}{22} +4 . 3\dfrac{1}{23} + \ldots \ldots .AGP$

$= 6 \left(4 - $\dfrac{11}{218}\right)

So,~mean of the new data~will be,

~$x = $\dfrac{12 - \dfrac{12}{240} + 2870 - 6\left(4 - \dfrac{11}{218}\right)}{20}

$⇒ x = $\dfrac{2858}{20} + \left(\dfrac{- 12}{240} + \dfrac{66}{218}\right) \times \dfrac{1}{20}

Now~$⇒ \left[x\right] = \left[142 . 4 + 0 . 00001\right] = 142$

$

questions.q: Consider a set of $3n$ numbers having variance $4 .$ In this set, the mean of first $2n$ numbers is~$6$ and the mean of the remaining $n$ numbers is $3 .$~A~new set is constructed by adding $1$ into each of the first $2n$ numbers, and subtracting $1$ from each of the remaining $n$~numbers. If the variance of the new set is $k,$~then $9k$ is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, the number be ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, . . . , {a}_{2n}, {b}_{1}, {b}_{2}, {b}_{3}, . . . , {b}_{n} .$

Given, the mean of the first~$2n$~numbers is~$6$~and that of the remaining~$n$~numbers is~$3,$~then by using the formula for combined~mean, we get, the mean of the complete set as~$\mu = \dfrac{2n \times 6 + n \times 3}{2n + n} = \dfrac{15n}{3n} = 5 .$

Also, the variance is defined~as~${σ}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ \left({x}_{i}\right)2}{n} - \left(\mu\right)$2$

$4 = $\dfrac{∑ \left({a}_{i}\right)2 + ∑ \left({b}_{i}\right)$2}${3n} - ( 5{)}^{2}$

$⇒ $\dfrac{∑ \left({a}_{i}\right)2 + ∑ \left({b}_{i}\right)2}{3n} =$29$

$⇒ ∑ \left({a}_{i}\right)2 + ∑ \left({b}_{i}\right)$2 = 87n . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, as per the given information, the distribution becomes

${a}_{1} + 1, {a}_{2} + 1, {a}_{3} + 1, . . . , {a}_{2n} + 1, {b}_{1} - 1, {b}_{2} - 1, . . . , {b}_{n} - 1$

Thus, the new variance is

$k = \dfrac{∑ ( {a}_{i} + 1{)}^{2} + ∑ ( {b}_{i} - 1{)}^{2}}{3n} - \left(\dfrac{\left(12n + 2n\right) + \left(3n - n\right)}{3n}\right)$2$

$⇒ k = $\dfrac{ \left(∑ \left({a}_{i}\right)2 + 2n + 2 ∑ {a}_{i}\right) + \left($∑ \left({b}_{i}\right)$2 + n - 2 ∑ {b}_{i}\right)}{3n} - $\$left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)$2$

$⇒ k = $\dfrac{∑ \left({a}_{i}\right)2 + ∑ \left({b}_{i}\right)2 + 3n + 2 ∑ {a}_{i} - 2 ∑ {b}_{i}}{3n} - $\$left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)$2$

On putting the given values and value from the equation~ \left($i\right),$~

$⇒ k = \dfrac{87n + 3n + 2 ( 12n ) - 2 ( 3n )}{3n} - $\$left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)$2$

$⇒ k = $\dfrac{108}{3} - \left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)2$

$⇒ 9k = 3 ( 108 ) - ( 16{)}^{2}$

$⇒ 9k = 324 - 256 = 68 .$

$

questions.q: If the mean deviation about the mean of the numbers $1, 2, 3, \ldots \ldots , n$, where~$n$ is odd, is $\dfrac{5\left(n + 1\right)}{n}$, then $n$& is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that mean deviation about the mean of odd natural number is given by& $\text{M.D} \left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{n}\left[\dfrac{n^{2} - 1}{4}\right]

So, now~\dfrac{1}{n}\left[\dfrac{n^{2} - 1}{4}\right] = \dfrac{5\left(n + 1\right)}{n}~(given)

$⇒ n - 1 = 20 ⇒ n = 21$

$
